name: Rosemary Vrablic

summary.text: Rosemary Vrablic was a managing director and private banker at Deutsche Bank who became Donald Trump's longtime banker and the Trump Organization's main contact at the bank after its commercial lending division stopped doing business with him, arranging hundreds of millions of dollars in loans on the private-banking side. She resigned effective December 31, 2020, after the bank opened an internal review of a real estate investment she and a colleague had made in a building partly owned by Jared Kushner. In 2023 she testified in New York's civil fraud case against Trump, describing the bank's pursuit of very wealthy clients as whale hunting and estimating the bank earned more than $6.8 million in fees from the Trump Organization in 2014. The Deutsche Bank file on this site records the lending relationship; this file holds what is specific to her.

facts.claim: Vrablic, a Deutsche Bank private banker and managing director, took over the bank's lending relationship with Donald Trump on the private-banking side after its commercial lending division stopped doing business with him, and she and colleague Dominic Scalzi resigned from the bank effective the end of 2020.
facts.quote: Deutsche Bank and she announced she was resigning effective December 31

sources.publisher: Yahoo News (citing The New York Times)
sources.title: Trump's longtime Deutsche Bank private banker and her close colleague abruptly resign

facts.claim: Before her resignation Deutsche Bank had opened an internal investigation into a real estate deal in which Vrablic and a colleague invested in an apartment building partly owned by Jared Kushner, according to reporting; the reasons for her departure were not stated at the time.
facts.quote: The bank had opened an internal investigation into a real estate deal in which she and a colleague invested in an apartment building partly owned by Jared Kushner.

sources.publisher: Yahoo News (citing The New York Times)
sources.title: Trump's longtime Deutsche Bank private banker and her close colleague abruptly resign

facts.claim: In November 2023 Vrablic testified in the New York attorney general's civil fraud case against Trump, describing the bank's pursuit of very high-net-worth clients as whale hunting, saying Deutsche Bank was the Trump Organization's largest single lender from 2011 to 2021, and estimating the bank earned more than $6.8 million in fees from the Trump Organization in 2014; she also described a Scotland golf-course loan the bank declined as Trump was about to take office.
facts.quote: she estimated the bank earned more than $6.8 million in fees from the Trump Organization in 2014

facts.claim: Trump's lawyers used Vrablic's testimony to argue that Deutsche Bank was eager for his business and knew to discount his statements of financial condition; Justice Engoron nonetheless found in February 2024 that Trump's statements to lenders were inflated, a finding the Appellate Division left standing in August 2025.
facts.quote: Trump's lawyers used her testimony to argue that Deutsche Bank was eager for his business and knew to discount his financial statements.
